prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2] SLA tiers (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Tier" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 93px
  col 2: header "Monthly uptime commitment" · longest unbreakable word 80px · one-line width 182px
  col 3: header "Service credit" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 88px
  col 4: header "Support channels" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 470px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 597px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 596px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r0C: widths [114, 203, 100, 179] · table 597×254px · row heights [53, 33, 94, 73] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1A: widths [114, 125, 90, 267] · table 597×214px · row heights [53, 33, 73, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [114, 125, 109, 248] · table 597×214px · row heights [53, 33, 73, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [114, 125, 100, 257] · table 597×214px · row heights [53, 33, 73, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [114, 110, 90, 282] · table 597×214px · row heights [73, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [114, 101, 109, 272] · table 597×214px · row heights [73, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [114, 101, 90, 291] · table 597×214px · row heights [73, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [114, 145, 90, 247] · table 597×214px · row heights [53, 33, 73, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
